feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The evidence so far: iteration 0 (±0.02 m, y=0.04, 0.18 m body, 0.8 kg) gave s-bend progress 0.185 with 2 line-loss events. Iteration 1 (±0.03 m, y=0.02) cut s-bend line loss to 1 but collapsed progress to 0.04, so the row change is a likely cause. Iteration 2 (±0.03 m, y=0.04, 0.14 m body, 0.6 kg, kp 2.5, base 1.5) had s-bend progress 0.1275 with line loss 1. Its two changes were made together, so the cause is not yet isolated. Your current proposal reverts only the body, so this race isolates it against iteration 2. I kept the iteration 2 controller so that the result reflects the geometry alone. Next race: if s-bend progress is at or above 0.15 and line loss is at or below 1, the lighter body was the cause of the drop, and the wider spread with the 4 cm row is good; then the sensor_size 0.016 test becomes appropriate. If s-bend progress stays near 0.13 with the baseline body, the wider spread is the cause, and the next step is to narrow it.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress is at or above 0.15 and line_loss_events is at or below 1: keep the body at 0.18 m and 0.8 kg, keep sensor_positions at y=0.04 with x from -0.03 to 0.03, and test sensor_size 0.016 to cover more tape at the edges. Evidence: iteration 0 (y=0.04, 0.18 m body) gave progress 0.185; iteration 2 (same spread, lighter body) gave 0.1275 with line loss 1, which points at the body change as the cause of the drop.

If s-bend progress stays near 0.13 (below 0.14) with the baseline body: narrow the spread to x = ±0.02 at y=0.04 with 10 mm spacing, keeping the 0.18 m, 0.8 kg body, to test whether the ±0.03 spread is what cost progress. Evidence: iteration 0 (±0.02, y=0.04) had progress 0.185 with the same body; iteration 2 kept the wider spread and reached 0.1275.

If s-bend progress is at or above 0.15 but line_loss_events stays at 2 on the s-bend or slalom: widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.036 m, keeping 15 mm spacing for the middle three, to keep the tape under a sensor at larger drift. Evidence: iteration 0 had 2 line-loss events per s-bend and slalom run at ±0.02 m, and iteration 2 at ±0.03 m reduced s-bend line loss to 1.
